title: Canadian C-Spine Rule
sources: Stiell IG et al. JAMA 2001; Stiell IG et al. NEJM 2003 (CCR vs NEXUS)
purpose: Determines whether a CONSCIOUS, STABLE adult trauma patient (GCS 15, no intoxication, non-distracting injuries) needs cervical-spine imaging. It is a 3-step algorithm — read the steps in order; the point tally here just flags whether imaging is needed.

items.label: STEP 1 — Any high-risk factor mandating radiography? Age ≥ 65, OR a dangerous mechanism (fall ≥ 3 ft / 5 stairs, axial load to head, high-speed MVC > 100 km/h or rollover or ejection, motorised recreational vehicle, bicycle collision), OR paraesthesias in the extremities

STEP 2 — Is there a low-risk factor that allows safe assessment of range of motion? Simple rear-end MVC (not pushed into traffic / hit by bus or large truck / rollover / hit by high-speed vehicle), OR sitting position in the ED, OR ambulatory at any time, OR delayed onset of neck pain, OR absence of midline C-spine tenderness

options.label: At least one low-risk factor present — proceed to Step 3
No low-risk factor → image the C-spine (stop)

items.label: STEP 3 — Ask the patient to actively rotate the neck 45° left AND right. Are they UNABLE to do so?

options.label: Able to rotate 45° both directions → C-spine clinically cleared
Unable to rotate 45° → image the C-spine

interpretation.label: No high-risk factor, a low-risk factor present, AND able to rotate 45° each way — C-spine cleared clinically. No imaging required; remove the collar
Rule not satisfied at one of the steps — obtain cervical-spine imaging (CT is preferred over plain films in most adult blunt trauma centres). Keep the collar until imaging is cleared

notes: Applies ONLY to: alert (GCS 15), stable, cooperative adults ≥ 16, injury within 48 h, no intoxication, no distracting painful injury, no known vertebral disease (ankylosing spondylitis, prior C-spine surgery, spinal stenosis). In head-to-head trials CCR was more sensitive AND more specific than NEXUS for clinically important injury and cut imaging rates. If the patient cannot be assessed (obtunded, intubated, intoxicated), the rule does not apply — image.
buildNote: 3-step algorithm — any step failing → image; the point values just drive the imaging/no-imaging output.
